name: old asphalt road: a calm, deliberately low-contrast surface (so the hero and objects read clearly) of one dark warm charcoal tone with a fine sparse grain of mid-grey aggregate clumps whose density drifts gently across tiles, rare light grey stones and rare dark tar spots; its unconnected edges are a chipped broken rim 1 to 3 pixels deep that varies continuously along the road, lighter broken faces on the far (north) rim, irregular rounded-off ends at dead ends and outer corners, and a dry dark-brown ledge 1 to 2 pixels thick with a broken soil shadow on the south side; laid as a road network with crossroads, dead ends and long straight 1-wide and 3-wide runs (cracks and potholes are separate decals)

surfaces.part: asphalt road patches on dirt ground (flat terrain tileset sheet)

answer.evidence: This is a terrain tile sheet: dark charcoal asphalt road shapes lying flat on a brown dirt ground, with grain texture, chipped rims and a thin dark-brown ledge shadow on the south edges. The silhouette is a full 368 px wide across rows 0-303, so it is a ground sheet and not a standing object. The road pieces are flat horizontal surfaces seen from above, with no vertical front face of 3 or more rows, no eave and no ellipse. They read as a top-down ground surface, which is correct for the terrain kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt body is one charcoal tone with sparse mid-grey grain, rare light stones and tar spots, so it has about 4 steps against the 5-6 of Beodeul materials. The paving reference has 7 visible tones per tile and the candidate has 4, though the grass reference has only 3. The rim and ledge are structurally right: a lighter broken north rim, a dark-brown ledge on the south side, and a tinted edge with 0% neutral dark pixels. These edges are only 1-3 px thick and use very few tones, with about 11 distinct colours across the whole piece. The surface is not flat, with only 3% near-flat coverage, but the grain is thin and uniform and there are no per-clump highlights or varied clusters. Beside the references the road reads as a single tone with speckle, which is slightly thinner and flatter than a careful artist would accept. The brief asks for low contrast, but the ramp depth is still short, so I fail it as borderline.
